text:
Samir Patel: dropped a quick mock for the Settings form 6 thinking about mixing inline validation with a compact top summary. thoughts? Jada Chen: +1 inline for field-level errors. but on long forms it gets noisy. worried about scanability. :thinking: Mike R.: inline is great for immediate fixes. for failures on submit we should focus on a summary that links to fields. keep error copy short. Toni M: accessibility note 6 if we do a summary it needs to be keyboard-focusable and announced via aria-live. also set aria-invalid on invalid inputs. Luis Gomez: another angle 6 destructive actions inside forms (eg delete workspace). we need a clear, low-friction confirmation. typed confirm for huge deletes, but for single-item deletes maybe an undo toast is sufficient. we had 3 accidental deletes last month in support. Samir Patel: idea: default = inline validation on blur, show compact error summary only on submit. required markers: subtle asterisk visually, but render an explicit screen-reader-only "required" for labels. Jada Chen: agree re asterisk. microcopy suggestion for summary: "We couldn't save \u2014 please check the highlighted fields." shorter than current. for delete copy, prefer "Type the name to confirm" when the data loss is irreversible. :thumbsup: Mike R.: mobile constraint \u2014 top summary eats vertical space. maybe collapse summary behind a banner with count "3 errors \u2014 expand" so we don't push content down. Toni M: code snippet for reference: ```
Enter a project name.
``` Toni M: using role="alert" + focus move to summary on submit helps screen reader users. Luis Gomez: for destructive flows I'm leaning to: small deletes = inline confirm + undo toast; bulk or irreversible = modal with typed confirmation + explain consequences. also ensure focus trap and accessible close. Samir Patel: good tradeoffs. i'll prototype three variants: 1) inline + expandable summary banner, 2) inline + persistent top summary, 3) inline-only + optimistic save with undo toast. will include a separate flow for destructive actions (typed confirm vs undo). Jada Chen: can you include copy options per variant? i'd like the UX Writing team to pick language. Mike R.: I'll validate with mobile breakpoints and show how the banner collapses. design-bot: New design doc created \u2014 https://redwood/designs/validation-patterns \u2014 includes accessibility checklist and metrics to track (error rates, dismiss actions, accidental deletes). Samir Patel: sweet. can everyone react to the doc with what they prefer? I'll sync with @UX Writing after protos. thanks all. :raised_hands:
